title: 🌫️ Study: Data-Center Electricity Caused About 650 Premature Deaths in America in One Year!
body: 🌫️ Study: Data-Center Electricity Caused About 650 Premature Deaths in America in One Year!

A new study by researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology revealed that pollution from the electricity consumed by US data centers in 2023 caused about 650 premature deaths, including 513 from fine particles and 137 from ozone — about 5.3% of all electricity-related deaths in the country.

Notably, the harm doesn't fall where the data centers are: although most electricity demand is concentrated in northern Virginia and Texas, the highest per-capita death rates were in Midwest states like Iowa, Nevada, South Dakota, and Kansas, because the interconnected power grid shifts demand to old coal- and gas-fired plants in the Ohio Valley.

The researchers explain that data centers consumed about 3.8% of America's electricity in 2023, and that rural residents face higher risk than city residents, because agricultural fertilizers in these areas increase the formation of fine particles in the air. The figures are scientific modeling estimates, not a count of actual deaths.

Lead researcher Noelle Selin says the impacts go far beyond data centers' neighbors, and that choosing a data center's location and electricity source should take air quality into account, not just land and energy prices.
Simply put: a data center in one state can pollute the air of another faraway state, because electricity travels through the grid, and smoke travels with the wind.
Did you know AI data centers have a health cost far from them?
